title: NASA Tests a System for Safer Moon Landings
paragraphs: NASA has tested a new system that could help spacecraft land safely on the Moon. It is called SPLICE. Scientists at NASA’s Johnson Space Center in Houston built it.

For the test, a small drone with four rotors carried SPLICE. The drone flew near NASA’s Armstrong Flight Research Center in California on 27 August 2026. It practised the movements of a landing on the Moon.

During the flight, SPLICE looked at the ground and made a detailed map. It checked for dangerous places, like rocks or holes. When a place was not safe, the system guided the drone to a safer one. NASA says the technology could help future missions to the Moon and to Mars.

questions.a: Scientists at NASA’s Johnson Space Center.

questions.q: What carried SPLICE during the test?
questions.a: A small drone with four rotors.

questions.q: What can SPLICE do when a landing place is not safe?
questions.a: It can guide the vehicle to a safer place.
